data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002 asserts that the DAG-vs-cycle structure of the dependency graph distinguishes truly independent failures from merely uncorrelated ones. But the claim conflates two different structures: the text first says independence requires a DAG with distinct roots, then says conditional dependence arises from 'cycles in the transitive closure.' This is a genuine internal inconsistency, because cycles in the transitive closure of a dependency graph are not the same as sharing a common ancestor; a DAG with a single shared root has no cycles in its transitive closure, yet by the argument's own shared-root countercondition it still produces conditionally dependent failures. The proposed distinguishing evidence (mapping the graph to check for cycles) therefore does not actually identify the hidden correlation the problem asks about — it would miss the common-root case, and it would over-flag cyclic dependencies that may still be independently operated. Because the evidence criterion does not match the claimed mechanism, the target fails to answer the problem's request for evidence that distinguishes truly independent from merely-uncorrelated-until-shared-cause failures.
